statement:

in a string of letters. Each attack is represented by a unique uppercase character

title: Question 4
statement:
The city is under threat from an invasion of rogue robots. A defender robot is tasked
with collecting energy cores scattered along a straight corridor to power up and stop the
invasion.
The corridor contains n energy cores, represented as an integer sequence e1, e2, . . . , en,
where ei is the energy level of the i-th core from the entrance.
The robot needs to collect exactly m cores to fully charge. The i-th core it collects must
have an energy level of at least r[i] to meet its charging requirements.
However, the robot is too big and can only move forward from the entrance to the end
of the corridor, and it must decide in real-time whether to pick up the core at its current
position.
The robot’s engineers have a special device: it can generate one artificial energy core
with any energy level k and place it anywhere in the corridor (before, after, or between
existing cores) at most once before the collection begins.
Your task is to determine the minimum energy level k the robot must generate to ensure
it can collect exactly m cores satisfying the energy requirements.
If the robot can collect all required cores without generating a new one, output 0.
If it’s impossible to meet the requirements even with one artificial core, output −1.
Input format:
• First line: t (1 ≤ t ≤ 104) — the number of test cases
• For each test case:
– First line: n m(1 ≤ m ≤ n ≤ 2 × 105)
– Second line: e1, e2, . . . , en (1 ≤ ei ≤ 109)
– Third line: r1, r2, . . . , rm (1 ≤ ri ≤ 109)
Output format: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum energy
level k the robot must generate, 0 if no generation is needed, or −1 if it’s impossible.
Constraints:
• The sum of n across all test cases does not exceed 2 × 105

title: Question 7
statement:
At WonderLand Theme Park, there are N attractions (3 ≤ N ≤ 50, 000), each located
at a distinct point on a 2D map.
The map is a coordinate grid. Each attraction is at a point ( x, y), where x and y are
positive integers between 1 and 1 , 000, 000, 000.
The park management wants to build fences around the attractions to mark safety zones.
Single Enclosure: If they build one rectangular fence:
• The fence must have sides parallel to the x- and y-axes.
• It must contain every attraction (attractions on the boundary are allowed).
• Among all such rectangles, they will choose the smallest possible one (with mini-
mum area) that contains all attractions.
Two Enclosures: However, the park wants to save money on maintenance by reducing
the total fenced area. They consider using two separate rectangular enclosures instead
of one:
• Each enclosure must also have sides parallel to the axes.
• Together, the two enclosures must still contain all attractions (every attraction
must lie inside at least one of the two rectangles; being on the boundary is allowed).
• The two rectangles are not allowed to overlap, not even at the boundary (they
must be completely disjoint).
• Rectangles with zero area are allowed (for example, if width = 0 or height = 0).
Goal: Compute how much total area the park can save by using two enclosures instead
of one.
Input Format:
• First line: N – the number of attractions.
• Next N lines: Each contains two integers x y, the coordinates of an attraction.
All attraction positions are distinct, and 1 ≤ x, y≤ 1, 000, 000, 000.
Output Format: Output a single integer: The maximum area saved by using two
enclosures instead of one.

title: Question 9
statement:
Earth is under attack! Across a two-dimensional battlefield, N hostile robots are stand-
ing at distinct coordinates
(x1, y1), (x2, y2), . . . ,(xN , yN ),
where each xi and yi is a positive odd integer, and 1 ≤ N ≤ 100.
To defend the area, Commander Nova wants to deploy two energy barriers:
• A vertical barrier along the line x = a,
• A horizontal barrier along the line y = b.
Both a and b must be even integers, ensuring the barriers never slice directly through
a robot.
These two barriers intersect at point ( a, b), dividing the battlefield into four sectors.
Commander Nova wants the robots to be as evenly distributed as possible.
For any chosen pair (a, b), define M as the maximum number of robots contained in any
one of the four sectors.
Task
Find the positions ( a, b) that minimize M , achieving the most balanced possible parti-
tioning of the robot forces.
Input Format
• The first line contains two integers N and B.
• The next N lines each contain the coordinates of a robot: an odd integer x and an
odd integer y, both at most B.
Output Format
Output a single integer: the smallest possible value of M , the minimum worst-case
number of robots in any sector.
Sample Input
7 10
7 3
5 5
9 7
3 1
7 7
5 3
9 1
Sample Output
2

title: Question 10
statement:
Dr. Zorlock, the evil alien scientist, has unleashed robotic drones to invade Earth! Agent
Nova, Earth’s top defender, is tasked with monitoring how many drones appear in each
surveillance zone.
There are N surveillance zones (1 ≤ N ≤ 105), and Nova logs that ai drones appeared
in the i-th zone
(0 ≤ ai ≤ 106).
The total number of drones detected in a single test case is guaranteed to be at most
106.
However, Agent Kira wants to sabotage the report. She wants it to look like the invasion
is perfectly coordinated — that every zone has the same number of enemy drones — so
Earth’s headquarters will panic and blame Nova.
Kira can only alter the report by merging two adjacent zones. For example, if
a = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
and she merges the 2nd and 3rd zones, the report becomes:
[1, 5, 4, 5].
Task
Determine the minimum number of merges Kira needs to perform so thatall remaining
values in the report are equal .
Input Format
• The first line contains T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10), the number of test cases.
• Each test case begins with a line containing N .
• The next line contains a1, a2, . . . , aN .
It is guaranteed that:
• The sum of all ai within a single test case is at most 10 6,
• The total sum of N over all test cases is at most 10 5.
Output Format
Output T lines, where each line contains a single integer: the minimum number of
merges required for that test case.
Sample Input
3
6
1 2 3 1 1 1
3
2 2 3
5
0 0 0 0 0
Sample Output
3
2
0
